label: Gothwal 2012
setting: Vision Rehabilitation Centres, LV Prasad Eye Institute, Hyderabad (low vision rehabilitation referrals)
diagnosis_mix: NR (diagnoses not reported; BCVA better eye >=20/60 17%, <20/60-20/200 58%, <20/200 25%; Table 2 p3)
recruitment: visually impaired adults (18+; BCVA better eye <20/60, or >=20/60 with restricted visual fields) referred to the Vision Rehabilitation Centres; sampling method and dates NR; 351 participants completed the instrument
notes: Rasch psychometric study, no sensitivity/specificity. Questionnaire given by trained interviewers face to face before examination (p2). VA: Bailey-Lovie logMAR chart, habitual and best-spectacle corrected, monocular and binocular (p2). Sex: 269 male (77%), 82 female (23%) (Table 2 p3). Mean better-eye logMAR 0.83 +/- 0.42 (Table 2 p3).

label: Wolffsohn 2000
setting: low vision clinic (Vision Australia Foundation; Melbourne)
diagnosis_mix: NR (conditions listed in Table 4 p8 as ARMD, glaucoma, diabetic retinopathy, other, multiple; counts not given)
recruitment: 515 consecutive first-time patients of a low-vision clinic sent the LVQOL before appointment; 65% returned pre, 83% of those returned post; 278 returned both (Table 2 p7)
notes: Development/validation and responsiveness study, no sens/spec. Age 78 +/- 11 and 34% male are for the 278 who returned both questionnaires (Table 2 p7); pct_female = 100 - 34 derived. Item-selection sample: 150 low vision patients (p3); normal-vision control group 70 (age 68.3 +/- 10.5, 39% male; p5). Administration by post, phone or in-person interview (p3). Completion time 5 to 10 minutes (p9). Best-corrected distance VA 0.56 +/- 0.34 logMAR in the 278 (Table 2 p7).

label: Labreche 2018
setting: university optometry clinics (Waterloo Optometry and Vision Science: Primary Care, Ocular Health, Low Vision clinics)
diagnosis_mix: NR (impairment groups only: central loss/VA/CS n=31; asymmetric acuities n=44; peripheral field loss n=10; any impairment n=60; normal n=29; Table 2 p4)
recruitment: consecutive from three clinics; sample deliberately enriched with visually impaired by recruiting from Ocular Health and Low Vision clinics; full eye exam within previous 4 months; telephone interviews May-Aug 2013 and 2014; retrospective chart review
notes: n_enrolled 93 = participants (p4); 1 excluded for not answering TICS-M, 2 did not complete VIRFQ, 1 declined all questions (p4). Abstract says 53 impaired + 33 normal (86), inconsistent with 89 in Results/Table 2 (60 + 29). Chart-review data; fields and stereopsis not measured in many; field defects mostly confrontation (p5). Median/mean age overall NR; per-group mean ages in Table 2 p4. 3 preliminary background questions A-C not analysed.

label: Rowe 2025
setting: stroke care (pre-hospital, acute and out-patient settings; guideline)
diagnosis_mix: NR (adult stroke survivors)
recruitment: NR (guideline based on systematic review; not a primary study)
cohort: CVSQ data come from a single primary study cited as ref 34 (Neumann et al.); 461 participants
notes: ESO guideline with systematic review of stroke vision screening; NOT a primary study (pitfalls 6). CVSQ accuracy rows are as tabulated in the guideline; primary paper not checked. No questionnaire-vs-LVR-need analysis; only accuracy vs specialist vision assessment. Other tools (V-FAST, VISA, MRFn, SVDST, Stroke Vision) are not self-report questionnaires and were not extracted.

label: Babcock-Parziale 2005
setting: veterans; inpatient VA blind rehabilitation center (Southwestern BRC; Tucson AZ)
diagnosis_mix: age-related macular degeneration 66%; glaucoma 10%; diabetic retinopathy 7%; retinitis pigmentosa 4%; other 13%
recruitment: veterans admitted Dec 2000-Jul 2002; VA-13 and FAST databases merged giving 190 matched cases; sampling method NR; all legally blind (20/200 or worse)
notes: Rasch psychometric study (retrospective pretest/posttest change; not diagnostic accuracy). Median age 77 (range 42-96); age mean/SD NR. pct_female = 100 - 93% male (p4). Central field loss 55%, peripheral 10%, both 14%, none 21%. Mean binocular logMAR of better eye 1.3 at entry, 1.2 at discharge (p4). VA-13 telephone by research staff 4-6 wk post-discharge (p2); FAST by clinician consensus; n_items and mode differ by instrument (VA-13 13, FAST 11 in text but 10 in Table p10). Language NR. Only VA-13 independence scale analysed (p2 footnote)

label: Oviedo-Cáceres 2023
setting: clinical practice guideline development (Colombian health system); no patient sample analysed
diagnosis_mix: NR
recruitment: not applicable: evidence-based guideline (GRADE, AGREE II, QUADAS, AMSTAR) with a group of 22 people with low vision and relatives rating outcomes (p3); searches Nov-Dec 2019 updated Jun-Jul 2020 (p3-4)
notes: no primary data and no accuracy analysis; recommends NEI VFQ for early assessment and follow-up of vision-related quality of life in patients >18 years with low vision (p5 Table 1; p10); published Rev Mex Oftalmol 2022;96(5) (journal header p4) although the screening record gives 2023; low vision defined as best corrected VA worse than 20/60 but equal to or better than 20/400 in the best eye or visual field <20 degrees in the best eye (p6)

label: Tabrett 2011
setting: hospital eye clinics and university eye clinic (low vision support and rehabilitation services; Essex County and Clacton and District Hospitals, Anglia Ruskin University Eye Clinic)
diagnosis_mix: primary ocular diagnosis, right eye (n=100): macular dysfunction incl. AMD 54; optic neuropathy incl. glaucoma 11; diabetic retinopathy 7; retinal incl. myopic degeneration 5; undiagnosed 8; cataract 2; corneal 3; other 10 (left eye: 57; 11; 8; 5; 9; 2; 2; 6)
recruitment: participants approached after attending low vision support and rehabilitation sessions; vision loss >6 months causing restriction in daily life; excluded: <18 y, unable to do verbal evaluations in English, no light perception both eyes, cognitively impaired (MMSE); dates and consecutive vs convenience NR
instruments: Activity Inventory; GDS; ISEL; AS-WAS; NEO FFI
notes: Not a diagnostic accuracy study: no sens/spec; correlations and regressions of Activity Inventory Rasch person measures with clinical visual function and psychosocial factors. Age median 81 (IQR 73-86) (Table 2 p3). Activity Inventory 30 goals and 235 tasks administered (p2); time 'approximately 35 minutes' typical (p2); mode of administration not stated (verbal evaluations in English required, p2). Distance VA binocular, habitual spectacles (p2). pct_glaucoma NR: glaucoma is grouped with optic neuropathy (11 per eye). Table 2 values are per eye for diagnosis but n=100 people.

label: Agathos 2025
setting: low vision rehabilitation clinic (Bicknell Envision Vision Rehabilitation Center; Wichita KS)
diagnosis_mix: age-related macular degeneration 116 (92.8%); hereditary maculopathy (Stargardt's) 9 (7.2%); glaucoma and other peripheral field loss excluded
recruitment: patients with binocular maculopathy and intact peripheral field referred to one clinician's low vision rehabilitation practice over one year; all invited agreed; no accuracy analysis
instruments: GAL-9; Falls and mobility screening questions G1-G5
notes: Not a diagnostic-accuracy study: no sensitivity/specificity against a reference standard; dta.csv empty. n=125 is the enrolled sample; ANOVA df F(2,97) on p13 implies about 100 patients with GAL-9 totals (unexplained). pct_female = (125-26)/125 derived from 26 males (p4). pct_glaucoma 0 because glaucoma patients were excluded (p4). Authors state they do not validate GAL-9 in AMD (p18). VA: ETDRS monocular, habitual correction; CS: LEA symbols binocular (p4)

label: Sahu 2021
setting: Low Vision Clinic of MGM Eye Institute (Raipur; Central India)
diagnosis_mix: NR
recruitment: consecutive; all patients referred to the Low Vision Clinic July 2015-Dec 2016 after ruling out treatable ocular condition; excluded prior LVA users, mental disability, unable to understand questionnaire, no light perception; 2 of 48 lost to follow-up
notes: pct_female = 19/46 (p2); age is 'average age at presentation' 29.2 years (p2), likely includes children; prospective pre-post study of low vision aids, not a diagnostic accuracy study; near VA analysed for 45 patients (p2); distance VA logMAR high-contrast chart, BCVA recorded (p2)

label: Wu 2016
setting: private ophthalmology clinics and medical retina clinics at the Royal Victorian Eye and Ear Hospital
diagnosis_mix: bilateral intermediate AMD 100% (glaucoma an exclusion criterion)
recruitment: prospective consecutive series; age 50+ with BCVA 20/40 (0.30 logMAR) or better and bilateral intermediate AMD (restricted range of VA)
notes: Online-first publication 2015 (Screening year may be 2016). No accuracy analysis; association of Rasch person measure with visual function in the better eye (study eye = better BCVA). n_enrolled equals n: paper states 100 included, enrolment/exclusion counts NR. 13 participants (13%) were non-drivers (p3).

label: Stelmack 2002
setting: two VA low-vision rehabilitation programs: VICTORS (Chicago Health Care System, West Side Division; partially sighted veterans) and Blind Rehabilitation Center (Hines VA Hospital; legally blind veterans)
diagnosis_mix: VICTORS (n=51): macular degeneration 39.2%; glaucoma 21.6%; diabetic retinopathy 17.6%. BRC (n=77): macular degeneration 66.2%; diabetic retinopathy 15.6%; glaucoma 11.7% (most frequent diagnoses only)
recruitment: consecutive patients admitted to each program; written consent waived by IRB; excluded severe cognitive or hearing deficits; 5 BRC veterans withdrawn and 2 VICTORS veterans died (p7); no masking
notes: Not a diagnostic accuracy study: Rasch analysis of NEI VFQ-25 plus 14-item supplement (39 items administered; 34 analysed after dropping 3 driving items and 2 items on 0-10 scale; p9) before and after rehabilitation, with instructions modified to allow low-vision devices (p8). Country not stated in text; sites named as Chicago IL and Hines IL (p6). Mean age VICTORS 68 (range 44-87), BRC 72 (range 38-88) (p7); age_range is the union of both ranges. pct_female = (11+5)/128 derived from p7 sex counts. pct_glaucoma = (0.216x51 + 0.117x77)/128 = 20/128 derived from p7 percentages. Mean best corrected VA 0.54 logMAR (20/63) VICTORS and 1.00 logMAR (20/200) BRC (p7). Whether the 128 are those left after the 5 withdrawals and 2 deaths is unclear; n_enrolled = n = 128 as stated in Abstract p1 and Subjects p7.

label: Stelmack 2006
setting: five sites: VA inpatient Blind Rehabilitation Center (Hines), VA outpatient low vision/eye clinic, and three outpatient low vision rehabilitation programs (VICTORS, Deicke Center, MEEI); veterans and private sector
diagnosis_mix: macular degeneration 69% inpatient BRC / 50% control / 67% outpatient; diabetic retinopathy 11% / 27% / 14%; glaucoma 8% / 8% / 7%; neurologic disorders 5% / 5% / 7%
recruitment: consecutive patients recruited at five sites May 2000-May 2002; 8 patients with serious health conditions and 11 with severe cognitive loss excluded by clinicians; control group = Hines VA waiting-list patients with test-retest only
notes: Responsiveness study not an accuracy study: no sens/spec and no reference standard; n=285 = 139 inpatient BRC + 116 outpatient + 30 control (p3; p3 text also says 136 inpatient); 3-month post-rehab telephone interview; n_enrolled not reported; age means by group 71 (SD 11.3; 42-87) inpatient BRC / 73 (SD 9.4; 49-88) control / 74 (SD 12.4; 27-90) outpatient; 93% male in inpatient BRC and control and 62% male in outpatient so pct_female NR overall; administration time 25-35 min (p5); habitual VA by best eye in Table 1 p3; same VA LV VFQ-48 items as the Stelmack 2004 validation sample (refs 9-12) possibly overlapping but not stated

label: Selivanova 2019
setting: vision rehabilitation clinic (Massachusetts Eye and Ear Infirmary, Boston)
diagnosis_mix: macular disease 56.0%; glaucoma 11.9%; optic nerve disease 5.50%; RP/peripheral retinal disease 10.1%; hemianopia 4.59%; other 11.9% (Table 1 n=109)
recruitment: prospective clinical cohort; new patients attending the clinic invited, Dec 2012-Dec 2014; adults, English speaking, no severe hearing or cognitive impairment; 219 declined; 189 completed pre-rehab questionnaires, 109 (58%) completed both
notes: Not a screening/accuracy study: outcome study of pre/post vision rehabilitation change in VRQoL (Rasch logits) and predictors of change (logistic regression, Table 3 p5); no sens/spec or AUC. n_enrolled = 189 who agreed and completed pre questionnaires (p3); n = 109 with pre and post (p3). Age is mean (SD) 68.5 (19.2); median 75 in Discussion p6; age range NR. Mode: mailed for self- or assisted completion, telephone if wished (p2); n_items NR as analysed form differs by subscale (IVI 28 items by item numbering p3; NEI VFQ-25 12-item functioning + 9-item socioemotional scales after Rasch item deletion, driving subscale not used, items A3-A5 added). Visual acuity: best-corrected, better eye, ETDRS logMAR, mean 0.52 (0.41) (Table 1 p4). Admin time NR.

label: Szlyk 2004
country: USA (sites: Chicago VA, Hines VA, Deicke Eye Center, Massachusetts Eye and Ear Infirmary, Boston)
setting: four vision rehabilitation programs: three VA/inpatient-type programs and private-sector low vision services (veterans and non-veterans)
diagnosis_mix: NR
recruitment: participants recruited from four rehabilitation programs: VICTORS Chicago VA (20), Hines Blind Rehabilitation Center (49), Deicke Eye Center (32), Massachusetts Eye and Ear Infirmary (16); sampling method NR
notes: Development/Rasch scale study; no sensitivity/specificity or accuracy against a vision measure; no VA or visual field data reported. pct_female = 20/117 computed from 97 men and 20 women (p3). Mean age 72 given only as an integer-valued mean (p3). Interviewer-administered by telephone before admission to rehab (p5). Country not stated explicitly; inferred from site names. Rasch analysis with WINSTEPS 3.16 (p5).

label: La Grow 2007
setting: older visually impaired people in a comprehensive low vision services study (pretest data)
diagnosis_mix: NR
recruitment: pretest data from both groups of an experimental/control study of comprehensive low vision services; selection process reported in another paper (ref 15), not here
cohort: pretest data of the experimental/control study in ref 15 (La Grow 2004), 186 older visually impaired people
notes: pct_female derived 128/184 (p2). Better-eye distance VA with correction: 107 between 20/100 and 20/200, 47 (26%) worse than 20/200, 30 (16%) between 20/40 and 20/80 (p2). 2 of 186 excluded for missing data on VFQ-25 or PQoL. 125 (68%) had other health conditions. Not a diagnostic accuracy study: hierarchical regression of PQoL on VFQ-25 (R2 change 0.050, p=0.001; p1-3); no sens/spec.

label: Gresset 2002
setting: community-residing elderly; home interview and home visual examination
diagnosis_mix: NR
recruitment: Stage 1: random sample of community residents aged 65+ in Quebec (CSHA 1991-1992; 1777 completed, 98.7%; ages 75+ oversampled). Stage 2 (validation): Montreal-area subjects not eligible for other CSHA components; all positives plus a random sample of negatives; 144 eligible, 31 lost, 42 refused, 6 unscheduled, 65 examined (45.1%); work-up (verification) bias acknowledged
cohort: Canadian Study of Health and Aging, Quebec community sample (stage 2 is a subsample of Montreal-area participants)
notes: Stage 1 sex: 1106 women and 671 men of 1777 (p3). Stage 2 age/sex of the 65 examined NR. VA ETDRS charts at 4 m (distance) and modified near ETDRS chart at 0.4 m; VA measured presenting and best-corrected; classified by best eye (p2). Examiner (first author) blind to questionnaire answers. Crude sens/spec cannot be applied to an unselected population because sampling fractions differed by test result (p2). Only functional (presenting VA) impairment tabulated, because after refraction only 2 subjects changed from mild impairment to none (p3). Paper title/abstract frames the study as prevalence and rehabilitation-service utilization; abstract PPV 21% and NPV 100% refer to moderate or worse

label: Murro 2017
setting: eye clinic (Local Centre for Inherited Retinal Dystrophies and Local Centre for Low Vision Rehabilitation; University of Florence)
diagnosis_mix: Stargardt disease (STGD) confirmed by genetic testing, all 16 patients with 2 ABCA4 mutations; mean better-eye ETDRS VA about 20/160 (0.84 logMAR)
recruitment: recruitment method NR (patients recruited at the two centres; no dates or consecutive/convenience statement)
notes: Both eyes analysed (31 eyes; one eye of 20/800 / 1.6 logMAR excluded as unable to read; p2); n is patients (16); analyses account for within-person correlation (p2). Age range includes a 12-year-old so not adults only. Sex: 10 female (63%), 6 male (38%) (p2). Not an accuracy study: correlations of NEI VFQ-25 composite with psychophysical measures. Administration: research staff explained and gave verbal instructions and assistance, completed questionnaires checked for missing data (p2); coded self.

label: Smith 2013
setting: outpatient or home settings (therapists' practices in 8 US states); online focus groups
diagnosis_mix: participants are 10 low vision therapists, not patients (7 females 70%; 3 males 30%; all but one a certified occupational therapist); no patient diagnoses reported
recruitment: purposive recruitment from colleagues; community low vision therapists; LinkedIn; conference contacts; 12 contacted and 10 agreed
notes: qualitative two-part study (therapist questionnaire then focus group) on LVIM clinical utility and content validity; no accuracy or psychometric data; each therapist administered LVIM to 6 clients (p6) but no client data reported; language not stated (assumed English; US)

label: Macnaughton 2019
setting: Vista low vision rehabilitation service, Leicestershire and Rutland (assessed at home 87% or Vista Low Vision Clinic 13%)
diagnosis_mix: AMD 50% (dry 10.17%; wet 20.33%); diabetic retinopathy/maculopathy 5%; hereditary retinal disorder 5%; retinal vascular occlusions 7%; glaucoma 12%; other 21% (self-reported primary cause, Table 1)
recruitment: newly registered (CVI) adults with visual impairment approached at referral to Vista; new to rehabilitation services; excluded if unable to complete assessments in English or cognitively impaired (Six-item Brief Cognitive Screener); sampling method (consecutive vs convenience) and dates NR
notes: Not a diagnostic accuracy study: no sens/spec/AUC; PAI evaluated by Rasch analysis and correlated with clinical and psychosocial measures. n=60 for PAI; ACC n=55, contrast sensitivity n=59 (p5). 47 goals retained after Rasch (p6). Binocular VA, habitual correction, Bailey-Lovie chart (p3). All interviews face to face by one examiner (p3). Time to administer NR.

label: Malkin 2013
setting: 28 private and hospital-based outpatient low vision rehabilitation centres
diagnosis_mix: macular disorders 55% (non-neovascular AMD 26%, neovascular 12%, other macular 17%) in the parent study; subset breakdown NR
recruitment: 77 consecutive participants (of 764 in parent study) who had EQ-5D collected late in the study; new LVR patients aged 18+, English telephone interview; 2008-2011
cohort: subset of 77 of 764 patients in the LOVRNET parent study (Goldstein 2012, ref 25)
notes: Responsiveness study, not a screening-accuracy study; no sens/spec. Median age 77 (Table 1 p3). Baseline and follow-up telephone interviews 6-9 months apart. Visual acuity only as categories in Table 1 (EQ-5D subset: profound 10%, severe 26%, moderate 34%, mild 30%); no reference standard used. n_items blank-equivalent NR: EQ-5D has 5 items, AI is adaptive (510-item bank).

label: Smith 2020
country: USA (therapists from six states; country not stated explicitly)
setting: home health agency or outpatient facility (occupational therapy low vision rehabilitation)
diagnosis_mix: macular degeneration n=24 (54.5%); cataract n=9; other n=5; glaucoma n=3; visual field deficit n=2; diabetic retinopathy n=1
recruitment: 8 occupational therapists recruited new clients from their caseloads (convenience); inclusion: diagnosed low vision from eye disease, good rehabilitation potential per therapist, new client; excluded if receiving rehab for other condition or not fluent in English
notes: Responsiveness study (pre/post OT), no accuracy vs reference standard; no VA measured (p6). pct_female = 32/44; pct_glaucoma = 3/44 computed; 1 participant gender not reported. 44 completed pre and post; number approached or enrolled NR. Therapists read items aloud (p3). Setting split 23 outpatient / 21 home (p5).

label: Wu 2026
setting: four U.S. institutions (setting type NR)
diagnosis_mix: macular degeneration 19.2%; glaucoma 16.9%; cataract 6.5% (primary diagnosis, not mutually exclusive)
recruitment: recruited June 2019-February 2022 to span a broad range of visual function (binocular VA -0.3 to 2.0 logMAR, mean 0.58 +/- 0.44); adults 18+, VA data available, English; cohort described in ref 7 (Wu 2024 TVST); fewer normally sighted people than general population (p8)
cohort: same 385 participants as Wu 2024 TVST (Screening ID 128)
notes: secondary analysis; items screened were single items, pairs, triplets, and the whole survey (p2-3). VA with habitual correction (Bailey-Lovie, ETDRS or Snellen); binocular VA used when available, else better eye (p2). Item performance estimated in context of full 100-item survey (p8). Age is mean +/- SD (Table 1 p3).

label: Chou 2009
setting: primary care screening (evidence review for USPSTF; included primary studies from clinic and community samples)
diagnosis_mix: NR
recruitment: systematic review of RCTs and 8 cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy studies (Table 4 p47-48); persons 65+ preferred, younger adults included if older-age data unavailable (p15)
notes: Review not a primary study (pitfalls 6): primary screening-question studies Hiller 1983; Eekhof 2000; McMurdo 1988; Teh 2006; Wang 1998 are tabulated in Table 5 p49-51 and were NOT entered as study 93 rows; extract from primary texts. Reports PLR 1.19-3.23 and NLR 0.23-0.78 for screening questions; DOR 1.60-9.45 (p20). Concludes no screening question accurate vs VA or ophthalmologic exam (p19). Table 5 (p49) gives per-question sens/spec but the extracted columns are scrambled

label: Massof 2007
setting: low vision clinic (Wilmer Low Vision Rehabilitation Service; Lions Vision Research and Rehabilitation Center; Johns Hopkins; Baltimore)
diagnosis_mix: 42% age-related macular degeneration; <1% other macular disorders; 11% diabetic retinopathy; 3% other retinal vascular diseases; 5% retinal degeneration; 3% retinal detachment; 4% other retinal disorders; 12% glaucoma; 6% optic atrophy; <1% amblyopia; <1% progressive myopia; 2% refractive errors; 4% CVA and brain disorders; 4% other disorders
recruitment: consecutive series of low-vision patients scheduled for a first visit, recruited to an umbrella research project (p1-2); no information on patients who declined (p2)
cohort: umbrella Wilmer low-vision measurement project; Activity Inventory sample (Massof 2005 refs 14-15)
notes: median age 75 (age_mean NR); 851 rated importance; 501 rated driving difficulty (p3); n=405 rated 21 driving tasks and contributed to the Rasch analysis (p3); binocular habitual-correction ETDRS VA median 20/60 mean 0.54 logMAR SD 0.45 (p2); Pelli-Robson log CS mean 0.78 SD 0.56 (p2); intake questionnaire by mail or telephone and AI by telephone interviewer (p2); no accuracy analysis

label: Subramanian 2006
setting: low vision clinics (Manchester Royal Eye Hospital; UMIST low vision clinic)
diagnosis_mix: bilateral ARM 76.2% (n=32); bilateral idiopathic optic atrophy 9.6% (n=4); bilateral ARM with glaucoma 4.7% (n=2); bilateral diabetic retinopathy 4.7% (n=2); bilateral macular holes 2.4% (n=1); bilateral resolved cystoid macular edema 2.4% (n=1)
recruitment: visually impaired attenders of two low vision clinics, some referred and some self-referred; better-eye VA 6/6-6/60 and poorer eye no better than 6/9.5; excluded if in hospital/nursing home, non-English speaking, or MMBlind <17/22; sampling method and dates NR
notes: Questionnaire development/Rasch validation plus correlation with vision tests; no accuracy analysis. 42 took part, 40 completed all experiments (p2); n_items 28 after Rasch reduction from 30 (p3) but text later says 26-item (p3); 15 min is an upper bound ("no more than 15 minutes", p3); median age NR; ages given as range 36-89 +/- 12.5 SD; pct_glaucoma = 2 of 42 with ARM plus glaucoma (p3); VA = ETDRS best-corrected binocular 0.47 +/- 0.30 logMAR; visual fields not measured (p2)

label: Di Maggio 2020
setting: three low vision rehabilitation services (Padua, Florence, Rome)
diagnosis_mix: AMD 58; myopic macular degeneration 27; diabetic retinopathy 21; glaucoma 14; miscellanea of acquired and inherited diseases 21 (counts as printed, n of 131)
recruitment: consecutive low-vision patients attending rehabilitation services in three centers (abstract p1); adults 18+; no selection on VA or disease (p2); dates NR
notes: No sensitivity/specificity/AUC reported; validation by Cronbach alpha 0.98 (p3) and Spearman correlations (Table 2 p4). BCVA linked for 106 patients, reading performance and contrast sensitivity for 76 (p4); n=131 is the questionnaire sample. pct_glaucoma = 14/131 (p3) = 10.7. pct_female 54 as printed (p3) but 75/131 = 57.3; diagnosis counts sum to 141 > 131. Same-day exam: ETDRS VA, Pelli-Robson CS, MNREAD (p2); VA eye/correction not stated except "best-corrected" (p4). The 60 min interviews were the translation-phase cognitive interviews, not administration time (p2).

label: Sumi 2003
setting: glaucoma patients followed at Tokyo Teishin Hospital or University of Tokyo Hospital
diagnosis_mix: POAG 69; NTG 56; primary angle-closure glaucoma 22 (of 147)
recruitment: NR whether consecutive; glaucoma only cause of VF/VA damage, followed >6 months, reliable HFA 30-2, no other physical impairment, VF stable >=2 years with controlled IOP
cohort: NR (developed on a separate sample of 102 glaucoma patients, Appendix p7)
notes: Prospective noncomparative survey (abstract p1). pct_female = 72/147 (p2). Mean best-corrected VA logMAR 0.3+-0.5 better eye, 0.9+-0.8 worse eye; mean deviation -11.2+-5.9 dB better eye, -17.4+-6.5 dB worse eye (p2). VF by HFA 30-2. Questionnaire is a validity study vs VA/VF correlation and regression; no sens/spec or screening threshold; n_enrolled taken equal to 147 (no exclusions reported)

label: Dickson 2012
setting: ambulatory office of a family medicine residency program (primary care; Wichita KS)
diagnosis_mix: NR
recruitment: consecutive-style: all patients presenting for care May-June 2011 who were 50+ and met inclusion criteria were approached; no cognitive or physical deficit impairing the tasks; $15 gift card; stopped at 69 enrolled; 23 randomised to each of 3 tests by drawing sealed envelopes
instruments: Functional Vision Screening Questionnaire; Mixed contrast sensitivity reading card; Snellen eye chart
notes: Time-to-administer study only; no accuracy data (paper states reliability to detect visual impairment was not assessed p4). 23 per arm; each participant did only one test. Questionnaire completed unassisted in private room (p2); card and Snellen administered by research assistant/standard practice (p2). time_to_administer_min = 186 s / 60 for the questionnaire (Table 2 p3). Age mean/SD/range and 77% female from Results p3. Language not stated.

label: Surawatsatien 2026
setting: ophthalmology clinic at a tertiary hospital (King Chulalongkorn Memorial Hospital)
diagnosis_mix: NR (retinal diseases most common concurrent ocular disease; baseline table in Appendix 1, not in text); better-eye vision impairment: none 245, mild 15, moderate 28, severe 1, blindness 12
recruitment: convenience sample, Feb 1-Mar 31 2024; 421 approached, 120 declined (refusal 28.5%), 301 interviewed at baseline; 275 completed 2-week follow-up
instruments: EQ-5D-3L; EQ-5D-5L; EQ-VAS; Vision bolt-on EQ-5D-3L; Vision bolt-on EQ-5D-5L
notes: Not an accuracy study: no sens/spec/AUC; psychometrics (test-retest ICC/kappa, known-groups, convergent Spearman, responsiveness) of vision bolt-on EQ-5D. n_items=1 is the added vision item. pct_female = 178/301 (Table 4 p7). Age/sex baseline table is in Appendix 1 (not in text); age groups in Table 4 p7. ~46% self-completed, rest read aloud by interviewer (p5). BCVA better-eye ICD-11 categories (p4). Bolt-on time 18-24 s (p10, Table 1 p6). Test-retest n=275 completers, but n in the ICC analysis (no-change group) NR; responsiveness better N=121, worse N=24 (Table 6 p9).

label: Pérez-Mañá 2022
setting: public hospital ophthalmology consultation (Hospital de la Esperanza, Parc de Salut Mar) and private ophthalmology clinic (Institut Català de la Retina), Barcelona
diagnosis_mix: visual impairment group (n=170): dry AMD 25.3% (n=43); exudative AMD 32.9% (n=56); cataracts 28.2% (n=48); glaucoma 11.2% (n=19); diabetic retinopathy 8.8% (n=15); other 12.9% (n=22); healthy controls n=195
recruitment: consecutive patients attending ophthalmology consultation; stable visual parameters (VA change <0.1 logMAR in last 6 months); visual impairment vs healthy groups defined by best-corrected VA (clear-cut cases and controls, authors note possible overestimation of accuracy); public hospital n=257 (119 VI, 138 healthy), private clinic n=108 (51 VI, 57 healthy); dates NR
notes: Overall age, sex not given: VI group age 78.8 +/- 10.0 y, 47.7% men/52.3% women (n=170); healthy group 68.7 +/- 11.5 y, 42.1% men/57.9% women (n=195) (p4). Public hospital patients did SLVQOL, NEI VFQ-25 and EQ 5D-5L by telephone; private clinic SLVQOL only, face to face (p3). Item 16 excluded from IRT/factor analysis (p6). Time to administer reported in seconds by subgroup (p5-6): see effects.csv. Case-control design with extreme groups; accuracy is of a QoL questionnaire total score, not a screening item.

label: Bibby 2007
setting: Low Vision Clinic of the University of Auckland
diagnosis_mix: various ocular conditions listed per patient in Table 1 (AMD, retinitis pigmentosa, glaucoma, cataracts, others); no percentages given
recruitment: 32 low vision participants recruited from the clinic; sampling method NR; 2 excluded because no longer visually impaired after recent cataract surgery
notes: Questionnaire administered verbally by an experimenter (p4). Vision measured binocularly with habitual correction (p3). Language of administration not stated. LCVA correlation used a reduced sample (Table 2 p4; 10 participants could not perceive any letters, p4); exact n NR. Table 1 p3 gives age and VA per participant only; sex not reported.

label: Wu 2024
setting: four US sites (University of Minnesota, Ohio State University, Johns Hopkins University, University of Alabama at Birmingham); clinic or phone
diagnosis_mix: top three diagnoses overall (Table): macular degeneration n = 74; glaucoma n = 65; cataract n = 25; other diagnoses not broken down
recruitment: participants from previous studies or patients at each site contacted by researchers; recruited Jun 2019-Feb 2022; no VA/field/diagnosis requirement so as to span a wide VA range (-0.3 to 2 logMAR)
cohort: same 385 participants as Wu 2026 (Screening ID 92); stated in Wu 2026, not in this paper; count as ONE independent dataset
notes: pct_glaucoma = 65/385 = 16.9 (derived from Table 'All' row); pct_female 57 as printed in Table. Administration by interviewer over phone or in clinic; survey took 30 to 60 minutes (Methods, VA Survey) - range only so time_to_administer_min = NR. VA mostly Bailey-Lovie or ETDRS charts, some Snellen (possibly 20-30%, Discussion), converted to logMAR; some VA from health records; eye and correction for VA NR. Inclusion: age 18+, VA available, English. Abstract says mean age 56.7 vs Table 55.71 (Table used). Paper does not state cohort overlap with other studies.
